changes.name: Episode 7 — Bannon, Peg & the Fog-Shits of Blackwake
changes.entry:
FOGPORT SESSION JOURNAL

Bannon, Peg & the Fog-Shits of Blackwake

Lantern’s Rest — Blackwake, Fogport

What began as an attempt to learn what Bellworks was hiding beneath a pumping station ended with a fake epidemic, an illegal weather spell, an evacuated city square, an industrial catastrophe, and half-drowned Thrallo crawling out from beneath the streets.

Byl Hasbaine and Lott still do not know exactly what they have stumbled into.

They know enough to be terrified.

BANNON & PEG

Byl and Lott needed access to the Bellworks pumping station without attracting attention.

Their solution was characteristically direct.

They bought pies.

While Byl distracted a Bellworks worker with theatrical charm, Lott quietly rendered the unfortunate man unconscious in Angelstab Alley. Byl took his uniform, checked his belongings, smeared grease around the unconscious man's mouth for reasons known only to Byl, and hid him safely beneath rubbish.

The worker's badge provided a useful identity.

Byl became Bannon, a miserable Bellworks laborer apparently crushed beneath the combined burdens of rent and employment.

Lott became:

Peg.

Their explanation was equally elegant:

“Pritch has the sicks.”

Specifically, the fog-shits.

Bannon and Peg were supposedly Crew Three replacements called in on their day off.

Somehow, this worked.

They penetrated deep into the pumping station and found the hidden experimental machinery.

THE SIXTH BANK

Beneath Bellworks they encountered Foreman Venn, Harl, other workers, and the experimental apparatus.

The machine was enormous.

Six cylindrical banks were being installed into it. Workers seemed to understand individual portions of the operation without understanding the whole.

Byl and Lott quickly discovered something disturbing: the people actually operating the machinery believed the safety bypass needed to remain open. Venn ordered otherwise.

Posing as a bored laborer, Byl pretended to struggle with the bypass wheel and announced:

“Bypass closed, Boss.”

He had actually left it open.

He also stole a blueprint.

When Byl decided their shift had abruptly ended—

“Time to go… Peg! We’re off the clock.”

—the disguise finally collapsed.

Venn ordered them stopped.

Bannon and Peg ran.

Before fleeing up the stairs, Byl emptied a bag of marbles behind them.

The pursuing Bellworks guards discovered several fundamental principles concerning gravity, glass spheres, and staircases.

Then someone seated the sixth cylinder.

The machine surged.

Because Byl had secretly left the bypass open, the excess pressure escaped through the old system instead of catastrophically destroying the pumping station.

Bannon and Peg had accidentally prevented an industrial disaster while attempting to sabotage one.

They escaped into the Lantern’s Rest crowds.

Lott's assessment:

“Good lie.”

RETURN TO THE TWISTED EEL

After scattering the stolen workman's uniform throughout Angelstab Alley, Byl changed back into his own clothing.

Once certain they were not followed, Byl and Lott returned to the Twisted Eel.

Mercy brought them into her office.

Byl froze the dampness around the room into frost to prevent eavesdropping.

They compared the stolen Bellworks blueprint, the workers' notebook, and Byl's father's old map.

The pieces began fitting together.

The machine was officially described as:

MUNICIPAL PRESSURE EQUALIZATION ENGINE — EXPERIMENTAL NO. 2

It connected to Fogport's forgotten municipal pressure network.

The notebook referred repeatedly to:

PRESSURE REVERSAL

and:

SUCCESSFUL EXTRACTION

The planned test area was:

B/W-7

Blackwake Sector Seven.

The old pressure lines converged beneath Gannet Square, where Byl's father's map showed something no longer present on modern maps:

BLACKWAKE MUNICIPAL WATER & DRAINAGE — RESERVOIR HOUSE

The modern building occupying that site was considerably more troubling.

It was the Blackwake Civic Vigilance district office.

Bellworks and Civic Vigilance were not opposing factions. They were both parts of the Civic Order.

Whatever was happening beneath Blackwake appeared to be a government operation.

Meanwhile, Batley had followed one of the mysterious black equipment chests from Bellworks directly to Civic Vigilance.

He had also seen Mr. Courier watching the Vigilance building.

The Courier was still withholding something.

THE EYE IN THE SALT

Time was running short.

The notebook demanded a successful extraction before a Civic demonstration, and Bellworks workers had repeatedly discussed an inspection.

Lantern's Rest was approaching its evening culmination.

Byl needed answers.

So naturally he ordered Batley's second-worst ale, drank the entire thing in one pull, stole a salt cellar from a neighboring table, and poured its contents across the wood.

He drew an eye in the salt.

Then slammed his face directly into the table.

Byl opened his mind's eye inside the Blackwake Civic Vigilance building.

The spell succeeded Fantastically.

He saw through the offices and into the old underground reservoir.

Bellworks equipment had been connected to the forgotten municipal works.

Black canal water filled the chamber.

Plans revealed the night's schedule:

8:00 — INTAKE
8:03 — REVERSAL
8:05 — EXTRACTION

The demonstration was to occur during the Lantern's Rest gathering in Gannet Square.

Byl overheard a horrified engineer ask whether the test would proceed with civilians present.

The answer from Civic Vigilance:

“That is the demonstration.”

The pressure reversal would create enormous suction through Blackwake's storm-drain network.

Anyone standing near an open drain could be dragged into the system.

Children would be especially vulnerable.

Then Byl saw Venn.

She spoke about proceeding despite the earlier sabotage.

And somehow—

Venn sensed him watching.

She turned directly toward Byl's invisible mind's eye.

“Someone's watching.”

The vision shattered.

Byl awoke in the Eel with a bloody nose.

The salt eye had turned black.

And a thin black ring had appeared around his fingertip.

A PROBLEM TOO BIG TO SOLVE

The group finally understood the immediate danger.

But they still didn't understand the conspiracy.

Who truly controlled the experiment? What was the machine actually intended to accomplish? Why was Civic Vigilance willing to endanger civilians? What was Venn? What did the Courier know?

There was less than an hour remaining.

Byl realized they did not need to understand everything tonight.

They only needed to ensure that Gannet Square was empty at 8:00.

And thus Byl Hasbaine devised perhaps his finest act of civic responsibility.

He invented a plague.

THE FOG-SHITS

The rumor was simple:

A new disease was spreading through Blackwake.

It was airborne.

It traveled in the fog.

Symptoms were gastrointestinal.

Extremely gastrointestinal.

People were instructed to:

GET INDOORS.
SHUT THE WINDOWS.
STAY AWAY FROM DRAINS.

Batley spread the rumor through newsboys, taverns and food sellers.

Mercy's street connections carried it elsewhere.

Nettle's people helped it travel through the alleys.

Signs appeared. Stories multiplied. Three victims became six. Then people were supposedly dying.

But Byl realized rumor alone might not empty Gannet Square quickly enough.

He had another idea.

A horrible idea.

MASS FOG-SHITS

Byl and Lott climbed onto the roof of the Twisted Eel.

Byl looked across Blackwake at Fogport's omnipresent fog.

“It's a kind of FOG… it's weather.”

Lott covered his nose.

Byl reached into the fog with wild Lumen.

He changed it.

The fog yellowed.

Then came the smell.

Sulfur. Sewage. Rotten cabbage. Something deeply, biologically wrong.

The fake plague suddenly had physical evidence.

People smelled the approaching fog.

Panic erupted.

Doors slammed. Windows closed. Vendors abandoned stalls. Lantern's Rest crowds began fleeing Gannet Square.

Byl continued pushing the spell until 7:45 PM.

Then his strength gave out.

Lott caught him as he collapsed.

But it was enough.

The rumor had become self-sustaining.

One citizen shouted:

“THE BLACKCOATS ARE TRYING TO KEEP US IN THE FOG!”

That particular variation proved exceptionally contagious.

Civic Vigilance tried ordering citizens to remain in Gannet Square.

The citizens demonstrated an unexpected unwillingness to contract explosive airborne diarrhea merely because a Blackcoat told them to.

Byl and Lott had done it.

They emptied the square.

THE ROOFTOPS OF BLACKWAKE

Byl was nearly exhausted, but he needed to see what happened next.

Lott carried him.

They traveled toward Gannet Square using the hidden city above the city: Gutterkin roof trails, smugglers' planks, maintenance gantries, cables and improvised bridges.

Gutterkin lookouts quietly guided them toward safe routes.

Eventually Byl and Lott crouched behind a warehouse parapet overlooking Gannet Square.

Below waited Bellworks technicians, Civic Vigilance officers, Foreman Venn and the machinery connected to the underground system.

The expected crowd was gone.

Venn was furious.

But the demonstration proceeded.

8:00 PM

INTAKE.

Every storm grate in Gannet Square rattled.

Black water surged beneath the streets.

8:03 PM

REVERSAL.

The drains began sucking.

Paper vanished first. Then leaves. Lanterns ripped loose. Crates scraped across cobblestones. Market umbrellas collapsed. A handcart began rolling by itself.

Dozens of storm drains were simultaneously pulling enormous quantities of air underground.

Had Gannet Square remained crowded, people would have been dragged from their feet.

Children could have disappeared into the drains.

Instead, the machine consumed rubbish.

Byl's ridiculous plague had saved potentially hundreds of lives.

8:05 PM

EXTRACTION.

The suction stopped.

For three seconds, nothing happened.

Then every drain in Gannet Square erupted.

Black water blasted upward.

Grates flew from their housings.

Something struck the underside of the central access hatch.

Once. Twice. Again.

Then something beneath Blackwake roared.

Byl and Lott remained hidden.

They had to see.

SUBJECT TWELVE

A huge hand emerged through the broken grate.

Then another.

A figure dragged himself from the flooded underground reservoir.

A Thrallo.

Around nine feet tall—normal adult Thrallo scale—but hideously emaciated.

Starved. Scarred. Waterlogged.

An iron collar surrounded his neck.

Broken chain hung from it.

Brass fittings had been driven into his flesh.

Then another Thrallo began climbing out.

And another.

Venn was not surprised by what they were.

She was horrified that they had escaped.

She ordered:

“CONTAIN THEM!”

The first Thrallo looked directly at her.

Recognition filled his remaining good eye.

He spoke:

“Venn.”

She knew him too.

But she did not call him by a name.

She called him:

SUBJECT TWELVE.

For a moment, her command seemed to affect him.

Then another imprisoned Thrallo shouted:

“KORR!”

A name.

Korr remembered himself.

He took the broken chain hanging from his collar and swung it into a Civic Vigilance officer hard enough to throw the man through a market stall.

The square erupted into violence.

Venn screamed:

“NO GUNFIRE!”

She wanted the Thrallo alive.

Lott drew Kils.

He looked at Byl.

“Help?”

And then Byl noticed one final figure.

Standing beneath an awning on the far side of Gannet Square.

Watching the disaster.

Watching Venn.

Watching the escaped Thrallo.

Mr. Courier.

WHERE WE STOPPED

Lantern's Rest, approximately 8:05 PM.

Gannet Square has been evacuated because Byl Hasbaine convinced Blackwake that the fog causes explosive diarrhea.

The Bellworks/Civic Vigilance experiment has gone catastrophically wrong—or perhaps horrifyingly right.

Several mutilated and apparently imprisoned Thrallo have emerged from beneath the streets.

One is named Korr.

Venn knows him as Subject Twelve.

Korr knows Venn.

Civic Vigilance is attempting to capture the Thrallo alive.

Lott has drawn Kils and wants to intervene.

Byl is exhausted from two major acts of wild magic, but conscious.

The mysterious Courier is watching from across the square.

And somewhere beneath Blackwake lies the answer to why the Civic Order had living Thrallo chained inside an old municipal reservoir in the first place.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS

  • What was the machine truly designed to extract?
  • Why were Thrallo imprisoned beneath Blackwake?
  • What was being done to them?
  • Why did Civic Vigilance intend to use civilians during the demonstration?
  • Why must the Thrallo be captured alive?
  • Who authorized the operation?
  • Why did Venn order the dangerous bypass closed during the earlier test?
  • What exactly is Foreman Venn?
  • How could she sense Byl's invisible scrying eye?
  • What is the black ring left on Byl's finger?
  • What does Mr. Courier know?
  • Who does the Courier actually work for?
  • Why did he hire Byl and Lott to steal the Bellworks strongbox?
  • Was the 8:05 disaster a malfunction—or was this the successful extraction?
  • And what else is still beneath Gannet Square?

FINAL IMAGE

Byl and Lott crouch upon a Blackwake rooftop.

Below them, festival lanterns float in black water across an abandoned square.

Civic Vigilance closes around three battered giants emerging from beneath the city.

Korr's broken chain hangs from his fist.

Venn is shouting for him to be taken alive.

Lott draws his cutlass.

Across the square, Mr. Courier watches.

And somewhere in the fog behind them, somebody is still screaming about the fog-shits.
